name: Tanapag
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Quackenbush, Edward Miller 1968, From Sonsorol to Truk: A Dialect Chain (PhD diss., 226pp; comparative phonology covering Tanapag); not readable online

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page tana1281 and reference record 123099 (Quackenbush 1968)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: alt names Northern Carolinian, Sprache der Marianen, Tallabwog; sole descriptive reference Quackenbush 1968 (Michigan PhD, 226 pp., OCLC 844956817, Google Books zHs-AAAAIAAJ) typed overview/comparative/wordlist, languages covered Sonsorol.. Tanapag.
Consonant inventory only; nothing on stress; cites only Ethnologue 18 and Jackson & Marck 1991.

sources.citation: Ellis, S. James. 2012. Saipan Carolinian, one Chuukic language blended from many. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii at Manoa. hdl 10125/100894
sources.note: Nothing on stress (the word does not occur). p. 129: prosody explicitly excluded ("Two other linguistic domains, discourse and prosody, have not been researched enough to be included in the scope of this study"); phonemic-inventory chapter is for southern SpnCRL, not Talaabog. Ch. 1 pp. 7-10 treats Tanapag/Talaabog as a separate language of Namonuito origin ([n] for *l/*n, [rh] vs [sch], [h] vs [s]). pp. 130-133 summarise Quackenbush 1968:31 phonology section as syllable structure, segmental phonemes and phoneme incidence -- no stress reported there either.

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. & Jeffrey C. Marck (with Jesus M. Elameto). 1991. Carolinian-English Dictionary. PALI Language Texts: Micronesia. Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press. hdl 10125/62861; DOI 10.2307/j.ctv9hvsnv
sources.note: No stress statement. Intro pp. xv-xvi: Tanapag dialect = descendants of Namonuito migrants, more different from the two southern dialects than they are from each other; TAN-labelled headwords. Entry 'Enne' p. 147: Tanapag dialect characterised by /n/ vs /l/ contrast and single /s/ -> /h/. 'The Sounds of Carolinian' is a letter-to-phone table; headwords carry no stress marks (acute = vowel quality).

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. 1984. Selecting an orthography for Saipan Carolinian. In Byron W. Bender (ed.), Studies in Micronesian linguistics (Pacific Linguistics C-80), 237-258. Canberra: ANU. hdl 1885/253371
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6192.S78x 1984); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6192 .S78x 1984
sources.note: No stress/accent mention. States that all three Saipan dialects (incl. Tanapag/Enne) share the same nine vowel phonemes, short and long.

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. 1983. The internal and external relationships of the Trukic languages of Micronesia. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The fullest comparative phonology of the Chuukic chain by the compiler of the Carolinian dictionary (who worked with Tanapag speakers); may state Chuukic/Saipan Carolinian stress or vowel-length/gemination facts that bear on it. Not on ScholarSpace.

sources.citation: Elameto, Jesus Mareham. 1977. Linguistic dimensions of vernacular education for Saipan Carolinians. MA thesis, University of Hawaii. hdl 10125/76092
sources.note: No stress/accent statement. pp. 24-25 give a 'Tanapag Enne Dialect' consonant chart and 2.5.1 sound differences (Tanapag retroflex /rh/ and /h/ where Oleai has /s/: haar vs saar 'nothing', raabut vs soobwut 'woman'); graphemes h, rh reserved for Tanapag.

sources.citation: Fritz, Georg. 1911. Die Zentralkarolinische Sprache: Grammatik, Uebungen und Woerterbuch der Mundart der westlich von Truk liegenden Atolle, insbesondere der Saipan-Karoliner. Berlin: Georg Reimer. archive.org diezentralkaroli00frit
sources.note: Notation only, p. 8 'Aussprache und Lautbezeichnung': German spelling used 'mit Akzenten auf den betonten Silben'; a geminate consonant may form 'eine betonte Silbe fuer sich, z. B. in mang'. No placement rule; Saipan Carolinian of 1911 undifferentiated by dialect; Tanapag occurs only as a place name in example sentences; scanned text drops the accent marks.

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. & Jesus M. Elameto. 1977. Toward an orthography of Saipan Carolinian. University of Hawaii Working Papers in Linguistics 9(1).

sources.note: Earliest modern phonological sketch of Saipan Carolinian written with a Tanapag-heritage co-author; an orthography paper is where a stress remark (whether stress needs marking) would appear. Not on ScholarSpace.

sources.note: Generative phonology of four Chuukic languages (Sonsorol, Chuukese, Satawalese, Pollapese per Ellis 2012 p. 65); Tanapag is not among the four, but Pollapese/Namonuito-area speech is the closest described relative and the study may state stress for the chain.

sources.citation: Quackenbush, Edward Miller. 1968. From Sonsorol to Truk: a dialect chain. PhD dissertation, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor. 226 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only descriptive reference Glottolog lists for Tanapag (site 8 'Saipan' in his 17-point chain); has a short phonology section (p. 31 ff.: syllable structure, segmental phonemes) that could carry a remark on stress/sandhi across the chain, although Ellis 2012 reports none.

KIR stress is assigned prior to final vowel deletion') concerns Kiribati (KIR), not any Chuukic language; the Saipan Carolinian chapter (Jackson 1984, held) has no stress statement.
